text:
lina: heads up — customer 'Orion' on private VPC pinged us about a 40% month-over-month invoice jump. they attached their cloud bill and it's a mix of GPU hours + a vendor license charge we normally pass through. can we align on a clean template for these cases? :thinking:
kevin: do we know if that GPU usage is reserved vs on-demand? might change how we credit commits.
sanjay: i'll pull the billing export and tag usage by sku. quick note — for cloud-hosted private deployments, we currently allocate committed discounts (CUD) at org-level; do we want a per-customer proportional allocation or keep CUD as a company-level offset?
ellie: legal prefers transparency. customers want to see "third-party license" line. but tax/resale rules differ by region, so sales may need to toggle 'resale' vs 'included' per contract.
ops_lead: cluster health note: we had two autoscale spikes last week due to a test job; that added ~120 GPU hours for that tenant during the billing window. looks like keepalive + cold-cache effects. we should add autoscale guardrail for private VPCs.
kevin: if we provide a proposal to the customer, suggest a reserved commit (3–6 months) for their baseline and a tiered pass-through for spike hours. example rough: baseline 40 GPUs reserved -> ~22% unit saving vs on-demand.
procurement: confirm vendor invoice pattern: we receive one invoice per account with lines like: 
```
Software license (per GPU/month): $1800
GPU capacity consumption (hours): 12,340 @ $0.45/hr
Support & maintenance: $2,100
```
procurement: license is invoiced as a lump monthly license in some regions, in others it's per-GPU-hour. that variance is the root cause of the surprise.
finance-bot: billing-export ready: gs://redwood-billing/exports/2026-11/tenant-exports/orion-2026-11.csv (checksum: abc123) :mailbox_with_mail: 
sanjay: i'll reconcile vendor invoice lines to our internal SKU map and push a delta report. plan: (1) identify vendor license lines, (2) split into "pass-through" vs "included" based on contract flag, (3) compute per-GPU effective unit price after CUD allocation.
ellie: on the CUD allocation methodology — recommend: allocate CUD proportionally to baseline reserved hours per tenant, not to burst. document it in the invoice notes as "Allocated committed discount." keeps spikes charged at on-demand.
lina: can we draft a sample invoice snippet and a short FAQ for sales? they keep getting asked why license is separate and why numbers differ region-to-region.
kevin: draft attached below — simple, explicit, and machine-readable for our billing pipeline: 
```
Invoice for Nov 2026
- Infra (GPU hours): 12,340 hrs @ $0.45/hr = $5,553.00
- Allocated committed discount (CUD): -$1,200.00
- Third-party software license (pass-through): $7,200.00
- KMS usage surcharge: $12.50
Total due: $11,565.50
Notes: CUD allocated proportionally to baseline reserved hours. License passed through at vendor invoice amount.
```
procurement: one more catch — KMS HSM ops incurred a non-trivial charge for this tenant. we bill KMS usage separately but we need to ensure we capture per-request encryption counts, otherwise surprises.
ops_lead: recommend caching keys and batching small requests where possible; also add alert when per-tenant KMS ops > 100k/day.
sanjay: i'll produce the reconciliation and a suggested handset of invoice fields by EOD tomorrow.
ellie: also checklist for sales enablement: 1) standard invoice template 2) region-specific resale guidance 3) commit sizing calculator 4) quick note about what we pass through vs absorb.
lina: perfect. once sanjay gives numbers we'll ship the template to sales and atomize the billing pipeline to emit the new fields. :thumbsup:
kevin: ack. thanks everyone.
